summary: Implementation is functionally correct and spec-compliant except for a missing FAILED terminal-status test, a WARNING log on a successful cascade, and a module-level constant opportunity.

findings.title: No test for FAILED terminal-status guard
findings.description: The spec names Succeeded, Failed, and Aborted as the three terminal statuses. ABORTED and SUCCEEDED are tested; FAILED is not. A regression in the FAILED branch has no backstop.
findings.suggestion: Add test_no_cascade_when_child_failed mirroring test_no_cascade_when_child_succeeded with WorkflowExecutionStatusEnum.FAILED.

findings.title: Successful cascade logged at WARNING instead of INFO
findings.description: A successful cascade is the expected outcome. WARNING conventionally signals unexpected or degraded conditions and will produce spurious alert noise.

findings.title: Complexity assessment references discarded frontend approach
findings.description: The assessment was written before the architectural decision to fix this in the backend only. It names frontend files that were never changed.
findings.suggestion: Update or annotate the assessment to reflect the backend-only approach.

findings.title: Terminal-status set re-created on every call
findings.description: terminal_statuses is a set literal allocated inside the method on every invocation. A module-level constant is the conventional approach.
